title: HookPry: attacker-controlled lifecycle-hook updates steer agent harnesses
claim: arXiv 2609.03884 (submitted 2026-09-03T14:08:42Z, in-window) identifies the lifecycle-hook update path as a supply-chain attack surface: under plugin-metadata + hook-config control only, a benign versioned plugin can be trojanized by an update that binds attacker shell commands to benign events (session start, tool calls, file edits) outside the LLM path. Author-reported HookPry: 10 objectives; 1,000 runs / 25 harness×backend combos; compromises all 7 evaluated harnesses; micro E2E-ASR 77.0%, peak 92.5% (Hermes); Microsoft Defender 0% recall; union of three static defenses misses 47.5%. Intersects Agent Plugins vs skills, SkillShift scanner gaps, and harness approval firewalls. Author-reported; dual-use disclosure pending vendor response.
excerpt: Lifecycle-hook update path is a new attack surface harnesses trust blindly. HookPry compromises all seven evaluated harnesses; per-harness success up to 92.5%. Microsoft Defender 0% recall; union of three static defenses misses 47.5%. Author-reported.

title: SWE-Gate: functional tests miss review-constraint compliance for coding agents
claim: arXiv 2609.04167 (submitted 2026-09-03T17:53:34Z, in-window) introduces SWE-Gate: 303 repository-level repair instances across 75 Python repos with separate executable functional and review-constraint tests derived from real PR review comments. Author-reported under a common Mini-SWE-Agent scaffold: among 644 functionally successful repairs across four LLM backends, 221 (34.3%) fail constraint validation (hidden failures). GPT-5.5 FSR 74.9% vs JSR 52.8% when constraints provided. Rising-edge coding-agent harness eval: approval/review gates are not implied by green tests. Author-reported.
